51615288.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to CM5 chip immobilized KEAP1 Kelch domain (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation equilibrium constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface plasmon: The Keap1 Kelch fragment was covalently bounded to the CM5 chip using coupling; the amines of the side chains of Keap1 reacted with the carbonyl group on dextran. We used an immobilizing buffer NBD (10 mg/mL, 1:20, pH 5.0) for immobilizing 1 mg/mL of Keap1 Kelch fragment protein. The SPR assay was performed at 25 °C on a Biacore instrument. The response values of the two channels Ch1 and Ch2 of the immobilized Keap1 protein were 4935.1 and 4929.3 RU (Resonance Units), respectively. Using PBS with 5% DMSO as a running buffer, we serially diluted the compounds six times by halving the concentration each time. The flow rate over the immobilized Keap1 protein surface was 30 μL/min. We analyzed the data using the instrument software.
original_paragraph.Results - Interaction of compound 9 with: We directly immobilized the Kelch domain on a CM5 chip, and the maximum immobilization response reached ~5000 RU. We prepared six separate solutions of the tested compounds (20, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25, and 0.625 μM) and passed them through the chip successively. Fig. 8 shows the SPR results. The Kelch domain fragment has a certain interaction with compound 9, and the curve was fitted according to the 1:1 kinetic interaction model; the dissociation equilibrium constant KD value was 16.47 μM.
original_paragraph.Figure 8 caption: SPR sensorgrams of compound 9 interacting with immobilized Keap1 Kelch domain. Compound 24 were tested over immobilized Kelch domain. Compounds were evaluated in 2-fold serial dilutions (1.25 μM, 2.5 μM, 5 μM, 10 μM, 20 μM). The data was fitted to 1:1 interaction model and the KD was calculated.
